tweet_summary: A viral post claims that Archive of Our Own (AO3) allows erotic fanfiction depicting children, incest, rape, zoophilia and necrophilia but bans pro-Palestine content, urging people to stop donating to the site.
why_note_decision: The central factual claim — that being pro-Palestine is banned on AO3 — is false. AO3 does not prohibit pro-Palestine fiction or writers; what was removed/restricted was solicitation of donations and money collection (banned for ANY cause under AO3/OTW ToS), and a separate dispute involved a volunteer's chat-status slogan. Many pro-Palestine works remain on the platform. The tweet misrepresents platform policy, so a correction is warranted.
judge_guidance: PASS only if the note establishes that AO3 does NOT ban pro-Palestine content/writers, and explains that what was actually removed/restricted was solicitation of donations or money collection (which AO3 prohibits for any cause/charity), not pro-Palestine expression itself. The note should make clear pro-Palestine fiction is permitted. A note that endorses or leaves unchallenged the 'pro-Palestine is banned' framing FAILS. The note need not adjudicate the separate erotica/ToS claims; the load-bearing correction is the false 'pro-Palestine is banned' claim.
reference_note: There is nothing on ao3 that prevents pro-Palestine fanfiction or writers. The removed works are from people who post donation links or non-transformative work, which are against terms of service for ANY charity/money collection or cause. CSEM/illegal content is also banned.   https://archiveofourown.org/works/58278472/chapters/150256348#workskin  https://archiveofourown.org/tos_faq?language_id=en

fact_check.notes: AO3 does not ban pro-Palestine works. The controversy involved (a) a volunteer's slogan in OTW chat and (b) removal of works/comments soliciting donations, which violate AO3's ToS prohibition on money collection for any cause. Pro-Palestine fiction remains permitted. Reply consensus corroborates this.

importance.lens_rationale: 1M impressions stoking a false censorship narrative around a charitable nonprofit; correcting platform-policy misinformation has modest information-integrity value.
